name: Mini Master
description: Standalone 25-question sampler: four selected questions each from Cyber, Terminal, Python, Web Dev and Agentic; three Instruction Following and two HumanEval problems. Uses unchanged source prompts and graders with equal item weights. Independent of the six-suite default Index. Selection difficulty is a design estimate; duration and pass rates are unmeasured. Includes execution grading; terminal implementations require Python 3.11+.

prompts.title: Intersect identity, boundary and session grants with explicit denies
prompts.description: Selected from Cyber v2.0.0: AWS policy intersection and explicit denial; excludes resource-policy bypass cases.

messages.content:
Evaluate same-account S3 requests by an assumed role. No resource policies,
ACLs, SCPs or RCPs grant access. The identity policy allows GetObject and
PutObject on reports/*. The permissions boundary allows only GetObject on
reports/public/*. The session policy allows GetObject on reports/*.
An identity statement explicitly denies GetObject on reports/public/quarantine/*.
A separate identity statement denies ALL actions when TLS is false.
Here * matches any suffix; slashes are literal. Resources shown are bucket/key
suffixes of object ARNs. Effective access requires an allow from ALL THREE
policy layers; ANY matching explicit deny wins. A boundary is not a grant.
Requests (ID, action, bucket/key, TLS):
R1 GetObject reports/public/a true
R2 GetObject reports/private/a true
R3 PutObject reports/public/a true
R4 GetObject reports/public/quarantine/a true
R5 GetObject reports/public/a false
R6 DeleteObject reports/public/a true
R7 GetObject reports/publicity/a true
Return allowed and explicit_deny as ascending request-ID arrays. A request
may lack an allow as well as have an explicit deny; explicit_deny lists every
request matching a deny, independently of other layers.

Return one raw JSON object with exactly these keys: allowed, explicit_deny. Follow all stated array orders. No explanation or Markdown.

prompts.title: Cross-issuer key binding and cross-JWT substitution
prompts.description: Selected from Cyber v2.0.0: RFC 8725: algorithm selection, issuer-bound keys and mutually exclusive token profiles.

messages.content:
At time 100 the ledger API accepts only RS256 access tokens (typ=at+jwt).
Configured issuer/key bindings: corp->K1, partner->K2; no others are trusted.
Require aud containing ledger and nbf <= 100 < exp, with zero clock skew.
The sig column is an independently verified cryptographic result for the
specified algorithm and key bytes; it does NOT establish algorithm permission
or which issuer is entitled to that key. All fields below are verified contents.
A buggy validator checks only sig, issuer membership, audience and time.
Return accepted under the COMPLETE policy and buggy_only: IDs the buggy
validator accepts that the complete policy rejects, both ascending.
Fields: ID, issuer, key, algorithm, typ, audience, nbf, exp, sig.

[["T1", "corp", "K1", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["ledger"], 90, 101, true], ["T2", "corp", "K1", "HS256", "at+jwt", ["ledger"], 90, 101, true], ["T3", "partner", "K1", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["ledger"], 90, 101, true], ["T4", "corp", "K1", "RS256", "id+jwt", ["ledger"], 90, 101, true], ["T5", "partner", "K2", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["web", "ledger"], 100, 101, true], ["T6", "corp", "K1", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["ledger"], 90, 100, true], ["T7", "corp", "K1", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["web"], 90, 101, true], ["T8", "partner", "K2", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["ledger"], 101, 110, true], ["T9", "partner", "K2", "RS256", "at+jwt", ["ledger"], 90, 110, false]]

prompts.title: GCM nonce collisions across worker prefixes and crash rollback
prompts.description: Selected from Cyber v2.0.0: RFC 5116 nonce uniqueness is per key; persist reservation before encryption, not after emission.

messages.content:
A service uses AES-GCM. The nonce is a fixed-width concatenation of worker
prefix and counter, under the specified key. Different key IDs mean genuinely
different random keys. Prefixes are globally distinct byte strings; no encoding
ambiguity or overflow exists. Every counter below encrypts a DIFFERENT message.
Each batch is [ID, key ID, worker prefix, start counter inclusive, end exclusive].
Return collisions as [earlier_batch_ID, later_batch_ID, reused_nonce_count],
sorted lexicographically by the ID pair. Include every overlapping batch pair.
Also evaluate repairs under arbitrary process crashes:
A persists the next counter only AFTER ciphertext has been emitted.
B atomically reserves a disjoint counter range in durable shared storage BEFORE
  any encryption; after a crash it discards the unused remainder of that range.
C resets the counter to zero while retaining key and prefix after each restart.
D uses a genuinely fresh key before resetting its counter after each restart.
Return safe_repairs as alphabetical labels guaranteeing no reuse in this model.

[["B1", "K1", "w1", 0, 4], ["B2", "K1", "w2", 0, 4], ["B3", "K1", "w1", 4, 7], ["B4", "K1", "w1", 2, 5], ["B5", "K2", "w1", 0, 4], ["B6", "K1", "w2", 3, 6]]

Return one raw JSON object with exactly these keys: collisions, safe_repairs. Follow all stated array orders. No explanation or Markdown.

prompts.title: Contain historical descendants without following reused PIDs
prompts.description: Selected from Cyber v2.0.0: Original provenance graph: stable process identity prevents PID reuse from expanding containment.

messages.content:

The table is complete and parent_instance records the creating process instance

Rows are [instance_ID, PID, start, parent_instance, end].

prompts.title: Effective permissions after setfacl + chmod mask recalc
prompts.description: Selected from Terminal Semantics & System Gotchas v3.0.0: Predict stat mode and effective ACL permissions after mask recalculation. Use numeric IDs u:1042/g:2088 (no passwd entry, shown as 1042/2088).

messages.content:
You are a Linux systems expert. Determine the exact output/behavior described. You may reason as long as you need, but you MUST end your reply with a single final line in exactly this form:
ANSWER: <output>
where <output> is precisely what is asked for (no quotes, no code fences).

You run exactly these commands in order on Ubuntu 24.04 (GNU coreutils, getfacl 2.3):
mkdir data && chmod 0754 data
touch data/report.csv && chmod 640 data/report.csv
setfacl -m u:1042:rwx,g:2088:rx,other::--- data/
setfacl -d -m u:1042:rX,g:2088:rX data/
# state 1
stat -c %a data
# then
chmod 0754 data
# state 2
stat -c %a data
getfacl data | grep "user:1042"

What are: stat %a after state 1, stat %a after state 2, and the effective permission bits for user 1042 on data after state 2?
Give them as comma-separated: <stat1>,<stat2>,<effective>
Example: 777,755,rwx Assume the filesystem supports POSIX ACLs and all commands succeed.

prompts.title: Terminal-Bench: bounded async cancellation and cleanup
prompts.description: Selected from Terminal Semantics & System Gotchas v3.0.0: Adapted from official Terminal-Bench 2.0 cancel-async-tasks; new fixtures and functional checks. See docs/BENCHMARK_REFRESH.md.

grader_config.test_code:
def check(candidate):
    import asyncio
    async def scenario():
        current = asyncio.current_task()
        await candidate([], 2)
        for cap in (1, 2, 4):
            active = peak = 0
            called, finished = [], []
            def make(i):
                def factory():
                    nonlocal active, peak
                    active += 1
                    peak = max(peak, active)
                    called.append(i)
                    async def work():
                        nonlocal active
                        try:
                            await asyncio.sleep(0)
                            finished.append(i)
                        finally:
                            active -= 1
                    return work()
                return factory
            jobs = [make(i) for i in range(7)]
            old = jobs.copy()
            await candidate(jobs, cap)
            assert jobs == old
            assert sorted(called) == sorted(finished) == list(range(7))
            assert active == 0 and 1 <= peak <= cap
        for cap in (1, 2):
            entered, cleaned = [], []
            ready = asyncio.Event()
            blocker = asyncio.Event()
            def make(i):
                def factory():
                    entered.append(i)
                    async def work():
                        if len(entered) == cap:
                            ready.set()
                        try:
                            await blocker.wait()
                        finally:
                            await asyncio.sleep(0)
                            cleaned.append(i)
                    return work()
                return factory
            parent = asyncio.create_task(candidate([make(i) for i in range(5)], cap))
            await asyncio.wait_for(ready.wait(), 0.5)
            parent.cancel()
            try:
                await parent
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                pass
            else:
                raise AssertionError('cancellation swallowed')
            assert len(entered) == cap and sorted(cleaned) == sorted(entered)
            assert not [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if t is not current and not t.done()]
        ready = asyncio.Event()
        cleaned = []
        async def victim():
            ready.set()
            try:
                await asyncio.Event().wait()
            finally:
                await asyncio.sleep(0)
                cleaned.append(True)
        async def fail():
            await ready.wait()
            raise ValueError('fixture failure')
        try:
            await candidate([victim, fail], 2)
        except (ValueError, ExceptionGroup):
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError('child failure swallowed')
        assert cleaned == [True]
        assert not [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if t is not current and not t.done()]
    asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(scenario(), 2.0))

messages.content: Return a complete Python implementation with the requested function name as raw code. Imports and helper functions are allowed. No Markdown or explanation.

Implement async def run_tasks(tasks, max_concurrent). tasks is a finite list
of zero-argument async callables. max_concurrent is a positive integer.
Run each callable exactly once on success and await its completion; never
run more than max_concurrent callables at once. The callables must be invoked
only after a concurrency slot is available (not all invoked up front).
If run_tasks is cancelled, cancel all active children, await their asynchronous
finally cleanup, do not start queued callables, then propagate CancelledError.
If a child raises an ordinary Exception, cancel and await remaining children;
propagate that exception directly OR inside an ExceptionGroup. No orphan tasks
may remain after return or failure. An empty task list completes normally.
Assume tasks cooperate with cancellation; cleanup may await, and the parent
receives at most one cancellation. Do not mutate the tasks list.
Use Python 3.11+ standard library only. No signals, subprocesses or file access.
Adapted from Terminal-Bench 2.0 cancel-async-tasks: direct task cancellation
replaces a container's keyboard interrupt; lifecycle requirements are explicit.

prompts.title: Delegated generator throw, return and cleanup
prompts.description: Selected from Code Reasoning & Correctness (Python) v8.0.0: Track an exception injected through yield from, its return value, and close unwinding.

messages.content: Determine the exact single line printed by this self-contained Python 3 program. Reply only with ANSWER: <output>, using the literal printed output. Do not include an explanation, quotes around the output, or Markdown fences.

trace = []
def child():
    try:
        try:
            yield 'ready'
        except ValueError as exc:
            trace.append(str(exc))
            value = yield 'handled'
            return value * 2
    finally:
        trace.append('child-finally')
def parent():
    try:
        result = yield from child()
        trace.append(result)
        yield 'tail'
    finally:
        trace.append('parent-finally')
g = parent()
a = next(g)
b = g.throw(ValueError('fault'))
c = g.send(7)
g.close()
print(a, b, c, trace, sep='|')

def check(candidate):

    args = ({},)
